acceptance: Preflight records effective Spark config at the three points for spark, and degrades with an explicit marker where reads are unsupported.
A tuning key overridden or refused by the engine appears as a discrepancy on the console and in the bundle; a clean run shows none.
A baseline (notuning) bundle contains the real effective state.
No credential-shaped value or absolute path leaks into the bundle, logs or anonymised export (tested).
Result schema change is versioned and documented; old bundles still load.
requested_config_hash and the drift marker are unchanged by the capture.
context: Origin: user requirement 2026-09-30 ("we must capture the actual state of the config during preflight for the run and highlight discrepancies"). Needs the runtime item's read-back hooks. Verify live: getAll() on Spark Connect, and what Sail returns.
description:
User requirement 2026-09-30 (must): capture the ACTUAL Spark configuration state during run preflight and highlight discrepancies. Configuration can be changed outside BenchBox (spark-defaults.conf, SPARK_CONF_DIR, cluster or service policy), so a ledger of what BenchBox asked for does not prove what ran. Today nothing reads the live session back; `get_platform_info` reports adapter fields, and spark.conf.set results are only recorded as "executed".

Design:
- Snapshot the effective session config at three points: (1) right after session creation, before BenchBox sets anything, to show what external config supplied; (2) after BenchBox has applied its settings (tuning, and for baseline only the harness-required ones); (3) at run start (just before queries) so late changes are visible. Use spark.conf.getAll() or per-key spark.conf.get; check availability on Spark Connect engines (Velox remote, LakeSail) and degrade explicitly ("not readable"), never silently.
- Compare: requested (tuning map) vs effective; BenchBox harness intent vs effective; external-supplied values that differ from the engine default. Discrepancy classes: requested != effective (override/refusal/immutable), external value present at snapshot 1, value changed between snapshots 2 and 3.
- Applies to notuning too: the baseline run must show the real default state.
- Surface discrepancies on the console at preflight and in the result bundle (a new block beside the applied ledger; extend the schema deliberately and version it). A discrepancy is a warning, not a failure, unless the user asks for strict mode.
- Redaction is mandatory: getAll() will include credentials (spark.hadoop.fs.s3a.*, tokens) and absolute paths. Apply the same credential-shaped key rules as the model item, and the anonymisation path used for the ledger, before anything is written to a bundle or log.
- Do not hash the full effective config into requested_config_hash or the drift marker; it is evidence, not identity (ADR-001). Decide whether a digest of the effective config belongs beside applied_ledger_hash.
- Tests with a fake session for each discrepancy class; live-Spark check for the real read-back behaviour.
